$comment: What this LAUNCHER installs, and what a check may believe about it.
`checked` is proved against this repository by scripts/manifest-is-true.sh;
`declared` is a statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
THE THIRD GRAMMAR, AND THE LAST OF THE THREE LAUNCHERS. estate-gates' C5
reads all three from one central file: `register <name>` out of a shell
script in stack-up, compose service keys in stack-single, Kubernetes kinds
here. One parser, three syntaxes, none of it living where the fact lives.
Now each launcher states its own, and the two readings can catch each other.
IT IS THE ONLY ONE WHERE THE ROUTINES ARE NAMED SOMETHING ELSE. A CronJob
here is called `crypto-trend` and the estate calls that routine
`qryx-trend`; `identity-sweep` is `idryx-detect`, `quality-drift` is
`verdryx-drift`, `drills` is `mockryx-drill`. C5 carries that map and its
comment says an unmapped routine is a FAIL rather than a skip, because one
it does not know is one it silently would not compare. The map is here too
now, as a pair per CronJob, so a rename on either side is visible from both.
SEVEN PERSISTENT CLAIMS, AND THEY ARE THE ONE THING IN THIS ESTATE THAT COSTS
MONEY BY EXISTING. A PersistentVolumeClaim provisions a real disk on every
provider and is billed from creation, whether or not anything writes to it,
and some providers round up to their own minimum so the requested size is
not always the billed size. 00-base.yaml says this beside the claims. They
are listed here so that adding one is a visible change to a file somebody
reviews, rather than a line in a manifest nobody diffs.
THE LOADBALANCER IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE DEFAULT INSTALL, for the same
reason: a cloud load balancer is metered. It lives outside the default
kustomization and stack-single reaches the same place with caddy, which
estate-gates already records as a recorded divergence rather than a gap.
distribution: ghcr.io/taipanbox/genaryx-console, built for amd64 and arm64 by .github/workflows/console-image.yml and merged into one tag (plus ghcr.io/taipanbox/stack-caddy and ghcr.io/taipanbox/stack-wg from tunnel-images.yml, same shape); manifests by tag, applied with kubectl or the install script

the_claims_are_metered.why: Each provisions a real disk and is billed from creation, whether or not anything writes to it; some providers round up to their own minimum, so the requested size is not always the billed size. Listed so adding one is a visible change to a reviewed file.

the_loadbalancer_is_excluded_on_purpose.why: A cloud load balancer is metered, so it sits outside the default kustomization and a default install never creates it. stack-single reaches the same place with caddy. estate-gates records this as a decision rather than a gap.

hub_entry_is_opt_in_and_metered.value: manifests/53-hub-entry.yaml (hub-ingress Deployment + type:LoadBalancer Service), applied by hub/up.sh
hub_entry_is_opt_in_and_metered.why: @decided 2026-09-26: a customer with several sites reaches one hub over outbound HTTPS to a single public entry, authenticated by the planes' own keys, with no VPN. Like genaryx-console-lb, this is a second type:LoadBalancer Service outside the default kustomization for the same reason: it is metered from the moment it exists (a GCP forwarding rule, about USD 0.025/hour) and Kubernetes provisions it, not Terraform, so it is deleted before a Terraform teardown (hub/down.sh does this first). Unlike every other opt-in manifest here, it also publishes a real product surface on purpose: exactly seven routes to tokenfuse-cloud and wardryx, held narrow by scripts/hub-entry-is-narrow.sh (invariant 23) rather than by being unreachable.

focus_export_runs_as_a_sidecar.why: It has no CronJob and cannot have one: it reads the gateway's local Parquet trace directory off disk, and that directory is an emptyDir, mountable only by containers inside its own pod by Kubernetes' own design. The other way out was to give it a PersistentVolumeClaim, which provisions a real disk billed from creation and is a spending decision rather than a fix.\n\nSo it is a sidecar in the pod that already holds the volume. It prints rather than storing, which is what quality-drift does one file over: in this deployment a routine's artifact is its log. Recorded as a GAP from 2026-08-06 until 2026-08-28.

costcrew_crew_moved_from_manual_to_routi.why: @yurii 2026-09-03, "do it all": un-suspend the crew CronJob, with the console's own cadence switch as the inner guard. costcrew v0.2.0's runner understands `-due`, so this CronJob no longer needs Kubernetes suspend to stay safe: it fires daily and `-due` refuses anything but cadence-due work with exit 2 (not a failure) unless a person has turned cadence on at the console's /cadence page, and never spends past the smaller of `-ceiling` and the console's own `cadence.ceiling_cents`. It is therefore no longer a Job TEMPLATE in Kubernetes' sense, and the manual_jobs bucket, which manifest-is-true.sh requires to carry `suspend: true`, would be false about it. Moved to schedules_routines instead.\n\nRecorded rather than resolved: estate-gates' C5 maps CronJobs to governance routines through its own ROUTINE_KIND, a table that lives in that repository, and `costcrew-run` is not in it yet. C5 will report `c5.routine-unmapped` for this pair until a person updates ROUTINE_KIND there, in a change to that repository, which this change does not make and this repository's own CLAUDE.md forbids making from here. Same shape as GOTCHAS 93: two correct rules, one repository apart, disagreeing until somebody closes the gap on purpose.

delegation_plane_is_opt_in.value: vouchryx (Deployment + Service + 3 NetworkPolicies + the vouchryx-state PVC), applied by delegation/up.sh
delegation_plane_is_opt_in.why: @decided 2026-09-27: the launchers offer vouchryx as an opt-in delegation plane, off by default, so a gateway can verify a proved delegation chain instead of trusting a claimed one. GOTCHAS.md entry 105 named the gap: with nothing turning it on, on_behalf_of travelled as a claim the caller wrote. delegation/up.sh refuses to apply anything until the operator supplies a trusted upstream issuer, audience and JWKS file (CLAUDE.md invariant 24; scripts/delegation-off-by-default.sh), mints vouchryx's signing key and revoke key once into the vouchryx-keys Secret (reused on every later run, never regenerated), and patches tokenfuse-gateway and genaryx-console with two kubectl patch --patch-file bodies (manifests/54-delegation-gateway-patch.yaml, manifests/54-delegation-console-patch.yaml) rather than a manifest kustomize applies, the same shape 55-copilot-cloud.yaml already uses. vouchryx-state is one more of the metered persistent claims 00-base.yaml's own comment already counts.

typryx_journal_is_on_the_shared_bus_and_.value: TYPRYX_EVENTS on stack-events (typryx.ndjson); tokenfuse-mcp-broker deployed with TOKENFUSE_MCP_UPSTREAMS=typryx=http://typryx:4320/mcp
typryx_journal_is_on_the_shared_bus_and_.why: @decided 2026-09-26: typryx's four event types (typed_answer, typed_unanswered, typed_refused, calibration_drift) are registered in agent-passport SPEC 6.2 (agent-passport#67, landed 2026-09-25), and typryx#6 lets a caller present its key inside a tools/call's own _meta object (TYPRYX_ACCEPT_KEY_IN_META=1), which is the shape the broker's TOKENFUSE_MCP_SECRETS vault already fills a {{secret:NAME}} handle into. So the journal moves onto the shared claim every other plane's history lives on, and tokenfuse's MCP broker (manifests/52-tokenfuse-mcp-broker.yaml, applied by the same --with-typed path) fronts typryx by configuration alone, nothing in tokenfuse's own code changes. Superseded: typryx_events_stay_off_the_shared_bus and typryx_is_not_wired_to_the_mcp_broker, both dated 2026-09-25; their text is not reworded in place, it stays in git history.
typryx_journal_is_on_the_shared_bus_and_.note: @claude 2026-09-26: moving the journal onto the bus does not make trailryx's own mapper seal it. The lines stop at the schema first (typryx writes agent-event/v1.0, trailryx 1.0 reads v0.1 to v0.3, so record-seal counts them unknown_schema; measured on stack-up 2026-09-26), and past the schema trailryx-agentevent refuses all four typryx types by name on purpose (trailryx#81) regardless of TRAILRYX_TRUST_DOMAIN (three carry a run id only when their caller passed one, and the fourth is a finding about a template rather than a run); record-seal counts a refused line and moves on. Whether trailryx maps them is that repository's own decision. The broker path needs typryx v0.2.0 or later (typryx#6); v0.1.0 refused every brokered call 401 (GOTCHAS 106). @measured on kind v0.33 2026-09-26 with typryx v0.2.0 pinned: an ask through the broker, its key only a {{secret:typryx_key}} handle, was answered and journalled on stack-events.

typryx_data_mode_is_chosen_at_deploy_and.value: typed/mode.sh (one copy for deploy.sh, deploy-gcp.sh, deploy-aws.sh): --typed-mode jev|own-model|off, default off; --with-typed alone renders manifests/51 and 52 unchanged (backend stub)
typryx_data_mode_is_chosen_at_deploy_and.why: @decided 2026-09-30: a customer chooses where the data of a typed answer goes from three modes (Jev, where the named fields of a question leave the cluster for TypeSafe's hosted API, a paid service; their own model on their own hardware, where nothing leaves unless the URL is a hosted service; or off), and the launchers ask. Jev and own-model are opt-in because each is a bill or a data-egress decision, so the default stays the free stub. The Jev key is a file the operator names, stored as the typryx-jev-key Secret and mounted as a file (TYPRYX_JEV_KEY_FILE), never an environment value, a ConfigMap or an argument. Each of the two real modes also renders one NetworkPolicy, typryx-egress-model, since 30-network-policy.yaml is default-deny. No new workload: typryx and tokenfuse-mcp-broker were already declared, so installs_services and persistent_claims are unchanged. Held by scripts/typed-mode-is-honest.sh (CLAUDE.md invariant 26).
typryx_data_mode_is_chosen_at_deploy_and.note: @decided 2026-09-30: --typed-training (off by default, any mode but off) sets TYPRYX_TRAINING_DIR, typryx v0.3.0's opt-in local training log, so a customer can fine-tune and calibrate a model of their own on their own data. Off, every render is unchanged. On, a mode gains that one environment variable and nothing else: the directory is /var/lib/typryx/training on the typryx-state claim typryx already had for its ledger, so persistent_claims is unchanged and no disk is provisioned (a claim is billed from creation, so a new one would be a spending decision for the operator). It lives as long as that claim and is not on stack-events. typryx is pinned at v0.3.0. @claude 2026-09-30: No cluster was used: the rendered manifests are schema-valid (kubeconform --strict) but a pod mounting the key Secret and an egress rule reaching a real model have not been run. @claude 2026-10-04: typryx is pinned at v0.4.0 since then, the release that adds the wardryx-proxy subcommand; v0.3.0 stays the first to read TYPRYX_TRAINING_DIR.

run_budget_ceiling_is_set_on_the_gateway.value: TOKENFUSE_MAX_RUN_BUDGET_USD=5.00 on the tokenfuse-gateway container (10-planes.yaml); --run-budget-ceiling USD on deploy.sh, deploy-gcp.sh and deploy-aws.sh changes it after the apply
run_budget_ceiling_is_set_on_the_gateway.why: @claude 2026-10-04: default 5.00 equals tokenfuse's own DEFAULT_RUN_BUDGET, so an ordinary run is unchanged and only a caller-declared larger budget is clamped (tokenfuse v1.5.0, invariant 73). It is not set on tokenfuse-cloud: tokenfuse does not clamp a budget the Cloud sets, and it bounds each run, not an agent's total spend. Held by scripts/run-budget-ceiling-is-set.sh and deploy-flags-agree.sh (CLAUDE.md invariant 28).

typed_risk_signal_is_opt_in_and_stateles.value: typryx-wardryx-proxy (manifests/56-typryx-wardryx-proxy.yaml), rendered only by typed/mode.sh --typed-risk-signal, off by default and refused when the typed mode is off
typed_risk_signal_is_opt_in_and_stateles.why: @decided 2026-10-04 (estate audit, wave 1, J2): a typed risk signal may turn a call into a hold for a person and never into a deny; its first consumer is wardryx (v1.2.0 hold_if_signal). The proxy is typryx v0.4.0's wardryx-proxy subcommand in the same image, answering from the backend the typed mode chose, with no claim, journal, ledger or training log of its own, so installs_services gains one workload and persistent_claims does not change. Only the MCP broker's TOKENFUSE_WARDRYX_URL points at it; the LLM gateway keeps asking wardryx directly. No hold_if_signal policy is seeded. Held by scripts/typed-mode-is-honest.sh (CLAUDE.md invariant 29).
typed_risk_signal_is_opt_in_and_stateles.note: @claude 2026-10-04: the proxy binds the pod address with TYPRYX_ALLOW_OPEN_BIND=1 because the broker can send no X-Typryx-Key, so its door is the one NetworkPolicy that admits the broker alone. estate-gates C5 will report typryx-wardryx-proxy as an unmapped service until SERVICE_KIND in that repository learns the name; this repository does not edit it. No cluster was used: the render is schema-valid (kubeconform --strict) and the proxy was run as a container against a stand-in wardryx, not in a pod behind these policies.

chain_verifier_runs_on_the_box.value: agent-conform, a CronJob every 15 minutes (40-routines-and-secrets.yaml), mapped to the routine agent-conform; state beside its output on stack-events
chain_verifier_runs_on_the_box.why: @decided 2026-10-04 (estate audit, wave 1, bus layer 3): every stream on the shared bus is a hash chain and nothing on a box checked one until agent-stack-go v1.1.0's `agent-conform watch-dir`; a break becomes a chain_broken event in agent-conform.ndjson on the bus, where heraldyx and the console already read. @claude 2026-10-04: a CronJob is a new pod per run, so its state (which findings it has already announced) cannot live in an emptyDir without a persistent break being announced every run, and a claim of its own would be a billed disk, so the state file sits beside the output on stack-events, which already exists: no new claim. A new break fails the Job on purpose. The verifier holds the bus read-write, so writing only its own files is the tool's own guarantee, not the mount's. Held by scripts/chain-verifier-watches-the-bus.sh (CLAUDE.md invariant 31).
chain_verifier_runs_on_the_box.note: @claude 2026-10-04: `agent-conform` is not one of the estate's routines yet. estate-gates C5 will report c5.routine-unmapped for this CronJob until ROUTINE_KIND in that repository maps it, in a change to that repository, which this repository's CLAUDE.md forbids making from here (the same shape as costcrew-crew, GOTCHAS 93 and 96); manifest-is-true.sh knows the name so the map here is checked.
